Container.Name: NexCraft-Daemon-Test
Container.Overview:
TEST STACK — runs the :test image (a feature branch), with its OWN data dir so it never touches your production NexCraft. Give this container its own IP and pair it with NexCraft-Web-Test.
The NexCraft daemon — the per-node agent that actually runs your Minecraft servers (downloads modpacks, bootstraps loaders, provisions Java, runs the processes). Ships with Java 21. After it's running, add it as a node in the NexCraft-Web-Test panel (default port 24444) using the access key from its data/Config/global.json. Docs: https://dpavlakis.github.io/NexCraft/
Container.Requires: Install the NexCraft-Web-Test container too — it's the dashboard that connects to this daemon. This is a TEST stack; keep its data separate from production.

Config.Name: Daemon Port
Config.Description: Daemon RPC port the panel connects to.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: TEST daemon data: instances, configs, the access key and (with the backup mount below) backups. Kept under nexcraft-test so it never touches production.

Config.Name: Backups
Config.Description: Where TEST instance backups are stored. Kept separate from production backups. Clear the field to keep backups inside the Data volume.

Config.Name: Instance Data Host Path
Config.Description: Host path to the InstanceData folder (used only by the legacy Docker-instance mode; harmless otherwise). Keep it pointing at <Data path>/InstanceData.

Config.Name: Docker Socket (optional)
Config.Description: Optional: only needed for legacy Docker-instance mode. Host/general process mode does not need it.
